releases.notes:
0.9.0 was tagged but never published, so these are its changes, first available in 0.9.1.

### New

- **Connect your bank with SimpleFIN.** On Import, paste your SimpleFIN setup token, click Connect, then Link accounts and sync. Accounts with no name match start on New account, with SimpleFIN's name and a guessed type, so saving without reviewing creates them. Change a row to skip it or link an account you have. A new account's first sync brings in the last 240 days; if SimpleFIN may have older history, the account says so, and a CSV import fills the gap. Linking an account that already has CSV history starts after its last CSV row, and a sync that still brings in rows matching your CSV says how many.
- **SimpleFIN syncs at most once every 24 hours, and that includes Sync now.** Sync now turns off with "Next sync in 22h" until the window passes. fi-fore also syncs once, quietly, when it opens and your bank data is a day old. A failed sync isn't retried for 24 hours; entering a new token clears that. If one bank needs a fresh login at SimpleFIN, only that bank's accounts show the error. The Days check-in strip shows "Synced today · next 22h", or "Bank data not updated" when the last attempt failed.
- **One Import page for every way in.** Import opens "Get your transactions" with Sync, Download and CSV. Once you're connected it leads with SimpleFIN, when it last synced and Sync now. Download says when it can't run, either because you're on a server or because your bank has no login address, and links to Bank setup. Clicking Import again brings the open Import window to the front instead of opening another.
- **Always categorize.** After you change a transaction's category, on Transactions or in Needs Review, fi-fore offers a rule for its description and says how many other rows it would change. The pattern is filled in with the description minus trailing numbers and dates ("VONS #2103 05/12" becomes "VONS"), you can edit it, and the count and a few examples update as you type. A rule matches any description that contains the pattern. A rule leaves rows you categorized by hand alone, and Undo removes the rule and its changes. Every import then applies your rules, and the result says "N categorized by your rules". The new Category rules page in Setup lists each rule with how many transactions match it now. Remove acts at once and offers Undo. Deleting a category your rules use is refused, with a link to those rules.
- **Starter categories.** A new household starts with Income (Paycheck, Interest, Dividends, Other Income) and about 30 spending categories, each already in Needs, Wants or Savings. A bucket fi-fore picked for you shows "Assumed" until you click Confirm. The import summary and Budget Rules › Category Mappings also have Confirm all, and Month Mix says how much of each bucket rests on assumed categories.
- **Transfers between your accounts.** On a transaction, choose Mark as transfer and pick the other account, or link two transactions that are the two sides of one transfer. Both sides stay in your balances and the transaction list, but leave spending, income, category totals and Needs Review. Marking or unmarking a transfer changes totals for past months too.

### Changed

- **First run leads with Connect your bank.** A new install opens on it: paste a SimpleFIN token, link your accounts, and your 50/30/20 split appears after the first sync. "No SimpleFIN? Import a CSV instead" is one link away, and Skip for now opens Days.
- **A household with no accounts and no transactions now opens on first run instead of Days**, including one that upgrades from an earlier version. Households with data see no change.
- **Setup's "Import & Connections" is now "Bank connections"** and only manages what is already synced: status, Sync now, Manage accounts, Disconnect and Unlink. Connecting a bank is on Import.
- **"Always categorize" replaces "apply to all matching".** The bulk recategorize prompt is gone.
- **Links to other websites open in your browser.** The app window no longer navigates away to them.
- The Import page is shorter: its method tabs and the top of the work area fit on a laptop screen, and a CSV's column mapping scrolls into view after you upload it.

### Fixed

- Mark as transfer works when an account name has stray spaces from a CSV, and a transaction can't be linked into two transfers at once.
- A category name, account name or bank message with quotes or markup in it shows as plain text instead of running as part of the page, in the category lists, Accounts, the Edit dialog and import messages.
- These fixes were in the 0.8.3 download but not in its notes:
  - Days: Cash Status shows each account type's own projection, so a credit-card forecast no longer moves the cash Projected EOM and a cash salary no longer moves the credit one.
  - Days: a transaction dated on a statement day counts once, so stepping from a closed month to the next shows no jump.
  - Days: the sub-menu jump links land in the right place, and the highlighted link follows the page order.
  - The plan ratio on Mix counts delayed and cancelled forecasts the same way Charges does.
  - Year shows its menu when you have no plan yet.

### Known gaps

- The cash-flow in and out totals still count both sides of a transfer.
- Starter categories are for new households only; an existing household keeps the categories it has.

### Security

- **Signed releases.** Every download carries a SHA-256 checksum file (`SHA256SUMS`), a Sigstore signature bundle (`SHA256SUMS.sigstore.json`) and a server-image digest pin (`*-server-image.txt`). Use the checksum commands and cosign instructions in the release notes to verify your download.

### New

- **A new way around the app.** On a computer, a sidebar on the left holds Days, Month, Year, What-if and Setup, and folds down to icons. On a phone, a bar at the bottom holds Days, Month, Year and More. Scenarios is now called What-if.
- **Setup replaces the Admin menu.** One page groups Accounts, Categories, Import & Connections and Bank Setup, your Budget Rules and Budget History, and Backup & Restore.
- **The Month page has three views: Charges, Mix and Cash.** Step through months with the arrows beside them, and the page keeps your view and filters. Charges shows what you expected against what happened, above your plan. Mix shows the month's 50/30/20 split, actual against plan, with what's left to spend in each bucket. Cash shows your balance looking ahead, up to five years. Filters stay in the address, so Refresh and Back keep them, and Budget breakdown opens for any month.
- **A check-in strip at the top of Days** says when you last reconciled and how many transactions are new, matched to your plan, or still need a look. "To look at" takes you straight to Needs Review, and Refresh data opens Import.
- **A quicker start.** A new household starts by dropping in a bank CSV: confirm the columns and see your 50/30/20 split for the months in the file, then add next month's plan.
- **Faster Needs Review.** Selected rows show an action bar that stays in view while you scroll. Each category has a select-all box, and Shift-click selects a range. Change a transaction's category right on its row. After an action the list stays where you were, and the reviewed list stays open.
- **Moving a match.** Matching a transaction that already belongs to another forecast moves it there, says "Moved from …", and offers Undo. Create Forecast tells you which forecast lost the transaction.
- **Find on page** in the desktop app: press Ctrl+F (Cmd+F on a Mac) or use Edit > Find.

### Changed

- **Category names ignore capitals and extra spaces.** "Groceries" and "groceries" are the same category, so you can't create both, and imported transactions spelled differently go into the category you already have. If you already have categories like that, the upgrade merges each set into one, keeping its transactions, forecasts, notes and sub-categories.
- Month and Year are always open, with a short "get started" message until there's something to show. The guide no longer talks about unlocking: "Unlock everything" is now "Skip the guide", and the Investment account type is always offered.
- Your plan lives in Month › Charges. The Forecast item is gone from the Days menu.
- The Create Forecast dialog has a cleaner look and picks the transaction's month for you.
- In the Import window, the links after an import open the page in the main window and close the Import window. Every import ends with clear next steps, including a folder import or a file with nothing new.
- Each release on the download site now lists checksums and signatures, so you can check that an installer is genuine.

### Fixed

- Renaming a category moves its transactions, forecasts and notes along with it. If the new name already had notes for a month, they're kept together.
- Cash Status on Days shows the balances for the month you're viewing, instead of $0 for any month but the current one. For a past month, Current Cash and Projected EOM are the balance at the end of that month, and Starting Cash is the end of the month before.
- Category notes show your text as soon as you save.
- After an action in the Categories section, Needs Review, the summary and cash position update to match.
- A transaction is never left matched to two forecasts at once, or to none, when two actions overlap.
- The match dialog ranks candidates against the transaction's real amount, a missed forecast shows "Missed" once, and double-clicking Mark reviewed reviews the item only once.

### Fixed

- **The header and navigation keep their look** when you move between pages. After clicking Months or Days, the page width, header border and nav buttons no longer fall back to unstyled.
- **In-app updates download.** The update banner's Download button now fetches the installer instead of failing with "status 404".

### New

- **One Categories section** on the Days and Reconciliation pages replaces the Category Breakdown and Category Reconciliation. Each category shows what you spent, the plan, how far over or under you are, how many charges, and how many items still need you. Expand a category for its sub-categories and items (open, matched, in budget, reviewed) with Match, Review and Create Forecast on each. On a phone, each category fits on two lines.
- **Create Forecast on any transaction**, including ones that are suggested or already matched to the wrong forecast. If the match can't be made, nothing is left half-done.
- **Undo a mistaken review** in Needs Review. Reviewed items leave Needs Review and match suggestions.
- **A shorter first import.** Create an account right on the Import page, and a single account is preselected. Column mapping collapses to one line when the columns are recognized, including named Debit and Credit columns. The preview says what will change ("812 new transactions across 5 accounts, 36 new categories, 1 duplicate skipped"), and a file with nothing new says so.
- **Transactions stored without an account** are assigned to the file's account when you re-import the same period, instead of being added twice. "Import all as new instead" keeps the old behavior.

### Changed

- Live Connections no longer mentions Teller or shows the administrator notice, and the empty state offers Import CSV. The Sync now button is gone until live bank sync returns in a later release.
- Category names are now unique across the whole category list. If you have two categories with the same name, the upgrade renames the later one.
- Month Summary totals and Cash Status skip forecasts you delayed or cancelled, and a delayed forecast counts in the month it moved to.
- Projected account balances count each scenario forecast once, on its own account type.

### Fixed

- **Import no longer drops real transactions.** The same charge on two accounts imports on both. Two identical charges on one day aren't merged into one when one is already stored. Renaming an account, or a case or spacing difference in its name, no longer causes duplicates.
- A failed import keeps your file so Retry works, and it no longer changes the account's last imported date or balance.
- The desktop app opens its own window even when another program is using port 3000.
- Deleting a forecast or a transaction also removes its matches, delays and cancellations, so a new forecast no longer inherits an old match.
- A delayed forecast keeps its account type, and you can't delay one from a month where it doesn't occur.
- Marking items reviewed reports the real count, reconciliation actions show readable messages when something fails, pages show the right title, and the Undo notice only appears after its reload succeeds.
- Reconciliation pages reject an invalid month in the address instead of showing it.

### New

- **Import a multi-account bank export.** When a CSV has an Account column, each row goes to its own fi-fore account. The preview asks you to match each account name it doesn't recognize to an existing account or a new one, then shows how many rows go to each account. Your matches are saved, so the next export from the same bank imports without asking. Descriptions no longer include the account name.
- **A clear summary after importing a CSV.** Instead of the preview, you see how many transactions were added, how many were already imported and how many rows couldn't be read, with Import another file, Reconcile in weekly check-in and See all transactions. If an import fails, Start over takes you back to the beginning.
- **Place new categories in Needs, Wants or Savings** from the import summary. Each new expense category shows its bucket (or Unassigned) with a picker that saves in place.
- **Update download progress.** While an update downloads, the banner shows how far along it is. A failed or stalled download says what went wrong and offers Retry.

### Fixed

- **Mark as Reviewed** in Needs Review works again, and a problem shows as a readable message under the section instead of a code error.
- The Days page and the CSV mapping screen now show the same "last imported" age.

### Fixed

- **Bank browser downloads work again.** Exporting a CSV or OFX from your bank shows the file name and continues to account selection and import. A cancelled or interrupted download shows an error naming the file, and downloads you don't import are cleaned up.
- **Import freshness** reads "0d ago" right after an import instead of "Unknown".
- **Dates show the right local day and month.** "Last imported" and "last synced" use your local day ("last synced" no longer shows "Invalid Date"). October no longer appears as September in Monthly Detail, the Credit view and the Scenarios item list. Month drill-downs on the dashboard and category statistics cover the month you clicked. "Today / N days ago" stays correct across daylight saving changes.
- **Imported categories count toward 50/30/20.** Categories created by an import are placed in Needs, Wants or Savings when fi-fore recognizes the name (Groceries in Needs, Restaurants in Wants, Retirement Contributions in Savings). Names it doesn't recognize stay unassigned.
- **Import page:** reloading the page no longer breaks Detect Columns. The intro only mentions what your version offers (the bank browser is desktop-only). The Transactions / Import / Forecast bar no longer floats over cards while you scroll. Text columns are left-aligned and amounts right-aligned in the mapping and preview tables, and a column's alignment follows its role.
- **Reloading any page** now gives a working page, not a bare fragment.
- The Days page loads without errors.

### ⚠️ Breaking: new database format

fi-fore now stores your data in SQLite instead of DuckDB. **Data from 0.6.x is not carried over:** after upgrading, fi-fore starts with an empty database, and backups made by 0.6.x (`.duckdb` files) can't be restored. Re-import your bank statements after upgrading.

### New

- **Self-hosted server.** Run fi-fore on your own server for several households, each with its own separate data. Includes sign-in, a first-run setup page that creates the first household, and a Docker image for amd64 and arm64.
- **Home Assistant add-on** that runs the same server.
- **Backup and restore on the server.** A restore takes effect right away, with no restart. Automatic backups are kept separately for each household.
- **Live Connections page** shows each linked bank's sync status and lets you disconnect it.

### Changed

- The database is now SQLite: faster, and installs cleanly on more machines.
- The importer is built into the app instead of shipped as a separate package.

### Fixed

- A fresh install no longer fails on leftover files from the old database format.

### New

- **Import a whole folder** of bank CSV files at once.
- Bank CSVs that begin with extra header text are cleaned up automatically before import.
- Each account's import status shows how fresh its data is, including an "Unknown" state when fi-fore can't tell.

### Changed

- The desktop window runs in a tighter security sandbox.

### Fixed

- Fixed an import error when marking a file as imported.
- Clearer feedback while an update installs, and a retry if the install fails.

### New

- **Bank integration.** Browse your bank inside fi-fore, map its CSV columns once, and import statements with their balances.
- **Guided mode.** A getting-started flow that opens up each page as you finish setting up the one before it.
- **Cash status on the Days page.** Shows money in, money out and how long your cash lasts, plus how up to date each account is.
- **Change a category everywhere at once.** Recategorize every transaction with the same description in one step.
- Reconciliation can match transactions automatically and lets you create a category without leaving the page.
- **Database recovery** if your data file is damaged, and a safer automatic backup when fi-fore closes.

### Changed

- Income and Expense categories always exist, so new transactions always have somewhere to go.

### Fixed

- The main window refreshes after you close the import window.
- Release pipeline improvements. No app changes.

### New

- **Installers** for Windows, macOS and Linux.
- **Automatic updates.** fi-fore tells you when a new version is ready and installs it for you.
- **Backup and restore** your data from the Admin menu.
- Sub-page navigation to move between related pages.
